videos.script: Lesson five chose technologies, and this one is about structure. {{title}} How a system is cut into parts, how the parts talk, and who owns which data. These decisions outlive any product you pick. {{five}} Not every one of them needs an architect, so we use three tests. Is it expensive to reverse, does it cross a team, and does it set a quality that several teams depend on? {{tests}} Then the trade-offs, because every structural choice buys one quality by spending another. A requirement like payments must be reliable cannot settle anything. {{reliable}} So we write it as a scenario in six parts, with a number at the end that someone can check. {{scenario}} Last, a decision with five criteria and three options: where should shipper invoicing live at Carreto? {{matrix}} A weighted matrix says the monolith. Then we move one weight and watch the winner change. {{sensitivity}} That crossing point is what to argue about, and the argument belongs to the people who own each side. Renata does not choose for them. Her job is to make the decision decidable. {{close}}
